text: Around this person, the things you would normally shrug off and leave behind refuse to stay left behind. Your Uranus is conjunct their Pluto: the part of you that breaks with the inherited version of things sits in the same place as the part of them that cannot let a matter be counted as small. There is no gap between the two functions, and no angle from which you can watch them separately. One caveat belongs early, because both bodies crawl. Uranus and Pluto hold a sign for years on end, so anyone born within the same stretch carries much the same angle between them. If your birth date and theirs are close neighbors, this conjunction is nearer to a description of those years than of the two of you, and you would find it again with half the people either of you grew up around. Put a wide span between the two dates and it stops being common weather and starts picking out this pair. Your two birth dates settle which it is. The aspect alone does not. From your side the effect is that your exits stop being clean. Your usual way of solving something is to cut it loose: change the terms, drop the tradition, refuse to hand on what was handed to you. In most company that works quietly. Here the thing you propose to drop turns out to be the one thing they cannot hold lightly. An ordinary refusal lands as a demolition, and you tend to be surprised by the size of what comes back. Running the other way, they give your freedom a weight it does not usually carry. You are used to walking out of arrangements without much ceremony. Near them, a break becomes an event with consequences attached, and whatever you left gets examined rather than simply forgotten. That is uncomfortable. It is also the part of this contact worth having, since a refusal you have had to account for is a different object from one you only enacted. In shared work the pairing is capable of real overhaul. Between you, the polite version of a problem does not survive long. You supply the willingness to scrap the design. The willingness to go all the way down to what the design was hiding comes from their end. Committees do not produce that. Two people with this contact sometimes can, and they can also take a working thing apart past the point where anybody knows how to rebuild it. The strain is that a conjunction offers nowhere to stand. Freedom and depth press on each other constantly, with no third function in between to absorb any of it. When it goes badly, each of you reads the other through the worst available frame: you look like someone who leaves, they look like someone who will not release. Neither description is usually accurate about anyone's intent. What tends to come out of this over years is a shorter and better list of refusals. The ones that were about something survive. The reflex ones do not last long in the company of a person who insists on knowing what a break is for.

You could know this person for years and never once use what stands between you. Your Uranus makes a sextile to their Pluto, which is an offer rather than a pressure. Your refusal to accept the received arrangement is within easy reach of the part of them that will not treat certain things as trivial, and neither function has to stretch to get there. The shape it takes when one of you does reach for it stays fairly consistent. They bring you something they are stuck on, a matter with more weight in it than it appears to have from outside. What you supply is not sympathy. It is the observation that the arrangement is not a law of nature and could simply be different. From most people that sounds glib. From you it sounds available, because you demonstrably live that way about something. They get handed an exit they had not been counting as an option. What comes back is that your detachment finds something worth spending itself on. Left to itself, the habit of not being bound to anything can quietly become a habit of not being for anything either. In their company the changes you would make in the abstract acquire a subject. You stop refusing in general and start refusing something in particular, which is a harder and far more useful thing to do. Practically, the combination suits any situation where somebody has to say the unsayable and somebody else has to mean it. Sorting out a family arrangement nobody has questioned in decades. Ending a working method everyone privately admits is finished. You provide the permission and the odd angle. The nerve to follow it past the point of discomfort is theirs. The characteristic waste with a sextile is that it never insists on being used. No crisis forces the discovery. Years can go by in which you know this person has depths and you never put anything of yours near them, because nothing in the aspect knocks. Each time it does get used, the tie thickens a little and stays thickened. What it becomes over a long acquaintance is a connection that can take a great deal of upheaval without either of you having had to fight for it.

Sooner or later you will want out of something this person is nowhere near finished with. Your Uranus squares their Pluto, so your instinct to break with an arrangement runs at a hard angle to their instinct to go further into it. No one here is choosing to be an obstacle. The two impulses simply do not share a direction. From your chair it feels like resistance with no argument in it. You point out that the whole setup is arbitrary, that it could be dismantled tomorrow, that nobody ever signed anything. What meets you is not a rebuttal. It is a weight, a refusal to treat the matter as light enough to be undone by a good point. You either push harder than you intended or you find you cannot say why you wanted out so badly. Neither response settles the question. From the other chair, it is not the change that stings but the ease with which you would walk away from it. You did not aim there. A square finds the sore spot by geometry rather than by intent. What you offered as a sensible change reaches them as a proposal to discard something they have staked themselves on, and their reaction is proportionate to that reading rather than to your sentence. The pattern worth watching is the one where the subject disappears. You get more radical, they get more immovable, and before long the question is no longer the one you started with. It has turned into a contest over whether anything is allowed to be permanent. Nobody wins that, because each of you is answering a different question than the one being asked. Giving ground does not end it. What ends it is saying what the break is for and what the holding is protecting, information the argument itself never surfaces. What the square is good for is that neither reflex gets to run unchecked. Your changes have to be worth their cost, because this person makes the cost visible. Their attachments have to survive being questioned, because you will question them. Pairs with this contact often notice, years on, that they threw away less than either would have alone and kept less than either would have alone, and were better served by both.

You do not have to talk this person into taking a drastic idea seriously. Your Uranus trines their Pluto, and the result is that your appetite for scrapping a thing and starting again meets no friction from the part of them that goes all the way to the bottom of what matters. Elsewhere your suggestions get softened before they get considered. People hear you propose ending something and immediately start negotiating a smaller version. This one does not. They take the proposal at full size, then supply what you generally lack: the staying power to see a change through its ugly middle, long after the interest of the idea has worn off. Uranus is very good at the break and much less curious about the far side of it. Their function is the far side. What you give them without effort is release. Depth with no exit available turns into repetition, the same matter worked over for years with no new move in it. You are the person in whose company an old fixation starts to look optional. You do not talk them out of anything. You visibly do not consider the thing binding, and being near that loosens a grip in a way that argument never manages. The risk in any soft angle is the missing brake, and here it has teeth. There is no pause built into this one. Your willingness to take a structure apart meets their willingness to go the whole distance, and neither of you supplies the objection. Decisions get made fast and thoroughly, and the two of you can leave a lot of wreckage behind while feeling entirely reasonable about it. If a plan of yours has never once met an obstacle in this person, that is worth noticing rather than enjoying. Where this pays over a long period is in anything that needs a clean break and a long follow-through at once: leaving a family pattern behind instead of passing it on, rebuilding a practice from the ground up, ending what should have ended years ago. You start it. They see to it that it actually finishes. Neither of you has to arrange that split, which is both the use of the contact and the trap in it.

Face this person across almost any question of what has to be kept, and the two of you will be holding opposite ends of it. Your Uranus opposes their Pluto. You carry the case for cutting loose. They carry the case for going further in. Each of you is holding the half the other has no instinct for. What stands across from you is a force that will not negotiate on your terms. You can be entirely right that a thing is arbitrary, inherited, and unnecessary, and being right moves it not at all. If your usual experience is that a sharp observation dissolves a problem, this is disorienting. It is also the most instructive part of the contact, because it separates the breaks you make because something is genuinely finished from the breaks you make because staying makes you restless. What they meet, over the same gap, is somebody their intensity does not capture. Most people either go under that weight or leave the room. You do neither. You stay, unimpressed, still visibly free, and that is an unusual thing to stand in front of. Whether it reads to them as relief or as provocation varies by the day. There is more than collision in it. Freedom with nothing at stake in it is only drift. Depth with no way out becomes a groove worn deeper every year. Between the two of you both terms stay in the room, which is uncomfortable in the ordinary sense and useful in the way oppositions tend to be: neither position gets to run the place unopposed. The failure mode is a permanent seesaw. You become the one who threatens to go and they become the one who will not let go, each of you performing a role the other's presence keeps producing. Once that sets in, neither is doing anything except acting as the counterweight. Standing nearer the middle is harder and considerably more interesting. It asks your refusals to name what they are for, and asks their attachments to survive being questioned out loud. That exchange is the whole value of the aspect, and nothing about the geometry makes it happen on its own.
